instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a workload on one Amazon EC2 instance that is built on the Nitro System. The instance boots from a separate root volume, and the workload keeps its data on one 2 TiB Amazon EBS data volume. The workload is a relational database with small, random reads and writes that needs about 10,000 IOPS. The company must choose the volume type for the data volume. Which volume type is the MOST cost-effective choice that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: A Cold HDD (sc1) volume, which has the lowest storage price per GB of all EBS volume types, sized to hold the data of the workload.

options.label: B
options.text: A Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volume, with IOPS provisioned for the busiest hour of the workload and kept at that level all day.

options.label: C
options.text: A Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume, sized so that its throughput matches the reads and writes that the workload performs each day.

options.label: D
options.text: A General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume, with IOPS and throughput provisioned above the included baseline only as far as the workload needs them.

items.stem: A company runs a database on one Amazon EC2 instance that stores its data on one Amazon EBS volume. The company accepts the loss of up to one day of data and a recovery time of several hours. The company does not run any of its instances across multiple Availability Zones today. The company must be able to recover the database if its Availability Zone becomes unavailable. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the data on the current volume. After a failure, detach the volume and attach it to a new instance in another Availability Zone of the Region.

options.label: B
options.text: Take a daily snapshot of the volume. After a failure, create a volume from the latest snapshot in another Availability Zone of the same Region.

options.label: C
options.text: Take a daily snapshot and copy it to a second Region. Keep a standby instance running there, and restore each new copy to its volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Take a daily snapshot of the volume and copy it to a second Region. After a failure, create a volume from the copy there.

items.stem: A company runs a media processing application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. Each instance writes many working files while it processes a job, and the job needs fast performance for small, random reads and writes. The files are temporary scratch data that the application can re-create from Amazon S3, and the storage must give the lowest latency possible. Which storage solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach a Cold HDD (sc1) Amazon EBS volume to each instance, and write the working files to that volume.

options.label: B
options.text: Launch the fleet on an instance type that provides instance store volumes, and write the working files to those volumes.

options.label: C
options.text: Attach a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon EBS volume to each instance, and write the working files to that volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Create one Amazon EFS file system, mount it on every instance in the fleet, and write the working files to it.

items.stem: A company launches Amazon EC2 instances from a launch template. Each instance has one Amazon EBS root volume, and the template keeps the default settings for that volume. When the company terminates an instance, the root volume disappears. An auditor now requires the company to retain the data of each root volume after its instance is terminated. What should the company change in the launch template for future launches?

options.label: A
options.text: Make no change, because Amazon EBS volumes persist after their instance is terminated, whatever the settings are.

options.label: B
options.text: Set the DeleteOnTermination attribute of the root volume to false in the block device mapping of the template.

options.label: C
options.text: Set the DeleteOnTermination attribute of the root volume to true in the block device mapping of the template.

options.label: D
options.text: Add an instance store volume to the template, and copy the root volume data to it before each termination.

items.stem: A company has taken a daily snapshot of an Amazon EBS data volume for the past year, and it keeps every snapshot. Snapshot storage costs are growing. The company needs to restore the volume to a point in time from any of the last 7 days, and it does not need older restore points. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Move every daily snapshot to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier, and restore an archived snapshot when the company needs a restore point.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep every daily snapshot, and copy the data to a smaller new volume, because snapshot charges follow the provisioned size of the volume.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy with a daily schedule and age-based retention of 7 days, and delete the older snapshots.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep every daily snapshot, because each incremental snapshot depends on the older ones and a deletion would break the newer restores.

items.stem: A company runs a PostgreSQL database on one Amazon EC2 instance. The database uses a 2 TiB General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon EBS data volume, but the volume holds only 200 GiB of data, and the data grows slowly. The company wants to cut the monthly storage cost of this volume. The database team accepts a short maintenance window. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a new 300 GiB gp3 volume, copy the data to it with a file copy tool, switch the database to it, and delete the old volume.

options.label: B
options.text: Modify the existing volume to 300 GiB with Elastic Volumes while the database runs, and then shrink the partition and the file system.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new 1 TiB gp3 volume, copy the data to it with a file copy tool, switch the database to it, and delete the old volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a snapshot of the volume, restore the snapshot into a new 300 GiB gp3 volume, switch the database to it, and delete the old volume.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region. Users upload images, and every instance must read and write the same set of image files with standard file operations. The solution must keep working if one Availability Zone fails. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the instance store volumes of each instance, and run a scheduled job on every instance that copies new image files to the other instances.

options.label: B
options.text: Create one Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume with Multi-Attach enabled, and attach the volume to every instance in each Availability Zone.

options.label: C
options.text: Create one Amazon EFS file system, and configure every instance to mount it at startup in each Availability Zone.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach a gp3 volume to each instance, and run a scheduled job on every instance that copies new image files to the other instances.

items.stem: A company runs automated tests on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in one Availability Zone. Each morning, on a predictable schedule, the company creates four Amazon EBS volumes from the same 50 GiB snapshot and attaches them to the fleet. The first test runs are slow, because the new volumes do not deliver their full performance at first. The volumes must deliver full performance from the first test run, which starts as soon as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Make no change to the process, because a volume that is created from a snapshot delivers its full performance as soon as it exists.

options.label: B
options.text: Create the four volumes as Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volumes with high provisioned IOPS, so that they start at full speed.

options.label: C
options.text: Write a script that creates the volumes each evening and reads every block of each volume with the dd utility before the tests.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable fast snapshot restore on the snapshot in the Availability Zone of the fleet, and keep creating the volumes from that snapshot.

items.stem: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances that store data on Amazon EBS volumes in one AWS Region. The company must back up the volumes every day and keep each backup for 30 days. Operators sometimes delete snapshots by mistake, and the company must be able to recover a snapshot that was deleted in the last week. The company wants to automate the solution. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Recycle Bin retention rule for EBS snapshots in the Region, with a retention period that keeps deleted snapshots for at least 7 days.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the volumes to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volumes, because their higher durability removes the need for daily snapshots.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy that targets the volumes by tag, takes a snapshot every day, and keeps each snapshot for 30 days.

options.label: D
options.text: Run a cron job on each instance that calls the AWS CLI every day to create snapshots and to delete the snapshots that are older than 30 days.

options.label: E
options.text: Rely on the replication that Amazon EBS performs for every volume, because it already keeps extra copies of the data for recovery.

items.stem: A company runs a mission-critical database on one Amazon EC2 instance that is built on the Nitro System. The database makes small, random reads and writes and needs about 12,000 IOPS. It needs low latency: the storage must give consistent sub-millisecond latency. The data volume must also have the highest durability that Amazon EBS offers. Which storage configuration is the MOST cost-effective choice that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Use two Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volumes in a RAID 1 mirror, and provision 12,000 IOPS on each volume.

options.label: B
options.text: Use one General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume, and provision 12,000 IOPS and the throughput that the database needs above the included baseline.

options.label: C
options.text: Use one Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volume, and provision the 12,000 IOPS that the database needs on that volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Use one Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume that is large enough to give the database high throughput for its reads and writes.

items.stem: A company stores customer data on Amazon EBS volumes and takes daily snapshots of them. All of the snapshots are encrypted with the AWS managed key for Amazon EBS. A new security rule requires a copy of each snapshot in a separate, isolated backup account in the same AWS Region, so that a compromise of the production account does not reach the copies. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Edit the key policy of the AWS managed key for Amazon EBS to allow the backup account, and share the existing snapshots with that account.

options.label: B
options.text: Share the existing snapshots with the backup account, and let the backup account copy them with a key that it owns.

options.label: C
options.text: Copy the snapshots with a customer managed key, give every account in the organization permission to use that key, and share the copies with all of them.

options.label: D
options.text: Copy the snapshots with a customer managed key, give the backup account permission to use that key, and share the copies with that account.

items.stem: A company runs an application on one Amazon EC2 instance that is built on the Nitro System. The application writes its data to a 500 GiB gp3 Amazon EBS data volume, and the volume is almost full. The data grows by about 20 GiB each week. The application cannot be stopped, so the team must add storage without downtime. Which action should the team take to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Stop the instance, detach the volume, and attach a new, larger gp3 volume that holds a copy of the data.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase the size of the volume with Elastic Volumes, and then extend the partition and the file system inside the instance.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a snapshot of the volume, restore the snapshot to a larger gp3 volume, and switch the application to the restored volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach an instance store volume to the running instance, and move the oldest data of the application to that volume.

items.stem: A company runs a clustered application on two Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are built on the Nitro System. Both instances are in the same Availability Zone. The application must be highly available, so both nodes must read and write the same block storage, and either node must be able to take over at once. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Format the shared volume with a clustered file system, and let the cluster software coordinate the writes of both nodes.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volume with Multi-Attach turned on, and attach the volume to both instances.

options.label: C
options.text: Format the shared volume with the XFS file system, and mount the file system on both instances at the same time.

options.label: D
options.text: Write new code in the application that coordinates every write of both nodes to the shared volume at the block level.

options.label: E
options.text: Create a General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume with Multi-Attach turned on, and attach the volume to both instances in the zone.

items.stem: A company runs a database on one Amazon EC2 instance that is built on the Nitro System. The database uses two io2 Block Express data volumes with 12,000 provisioned IOPS each. The instance type supports at most 15,000 IOPS for Amazon EBS traffic. Monitoring shows that the database reaches about 15,000 IOPS in total. However, neither volume reaches its provisioned IOPS. The team must raise the I/O performance of the database. Which solution is the MOST operationally efficient way to meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the instance to a larger Nitro-based instance type whose EBS limit is higher than the total provisioned IOPS of both volumes.

options.label: B
options.text: Move half of the data to a second instance of the same type with one of the volumes, and change the application to split its queries.

options.label: C
options.text: Raise the provisioned IOPS of both io2 Block Express volumes with Elastic Volumes, so that each volume has more IOPS than the database needs.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a third io2 Block Express volume, and stripe the three volumes in a RAID 0 array so that their IOPS add up for the database.

items.stem: A company runs a workload on one Amazon EC2 instance that is built on the Nitro System. The instance boots from a separate root volume, and the workload keeps its data on one 2 TiB Amazon EBS data volume. The workload is a log processing job that reads large files sequentially many times a day and must finish each scan quickly. The company must choose the volume type for the data volume. Which volume type is the MOST cost-effective choice that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: A Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume, sized so that its throughput matches the reads and writes that the workload performs each day.

options.label: B
options.text: A General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume, with IOPS and throughput provisioned above the included baseline only as far as the workload needs them.

options.label: C
options.text: A Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volume, with IOPS provisioned for the busiest hour of the workload and kept at that level all day.

options.label: D
options.text: A Cold HDD (sc1) volume, which has the lowest storage price per GB of all EBS volume types, sized to hold the data of the workload.

items.stem: A company runs a MySQL database on one Amazon EC2 instance. The database stores its data on a 100 GiB General Purpose SSD (gp2) Amazon EBS volume. After a product launch, the database needs 8,000 IOPS, but the volume does not deliver that many IOPS. The data will stay near 100 GiB for the next year. The change must cause minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach more gp2 volumes, build a RAID 0 array across all of them, and move the database files to the array to add their IOPS.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the volume type to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) with Elastic Volumes while the database runs, and provision 8,000 IOPS.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the size of the gp2 volume with Elastic Volumes until its baseline performance reaches 8,000 IOPS, and keep the gp2 volume type.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the volume type to gp3 with Elastic Volumes while the database runs, and provision 8,000 IOPS on the same 100 GiB volume.

items.stem: A company runs a media processing application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. Each instance writes many working files while it processes a job, and the job needs fast performance for small, random reads and writes. The company must make sure that the files are still there after the instances are stopped and started again for maintenance every weekend. Which storage solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon EBS volume to each instance, and write the working files to that volume.

options.label: B
options.text: Launch the fleet on an instance type that provides instance store volumes, and write the working files to those volumes.

options.label: C
options.text: Attach a Cold HDD (sc1) Amazon EBS volume to each instance, and write the working files to that volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Create one Amazon EFS file system, mount it on every instance in the fleet, and write the working files to it.

items.stem: A company stores financial records on Amazon EBS volumes in one AWS Region and takes a monthly snapshot of each volume. An auditor requires that each monthly snapshot is immutable for one year after the company creates it. Several administrators in the company's AWS account have full access to Amazon EC2. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach an IAM policy to every user and role that denies the ec2:DeleteSnapshot action on the monthly snapshots for one year.

options.label: B
options.text: Lock each monthly snapshot in governance mode for one year, with the lock set as soon as the company creates the snapshot.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Recycle Bin retention rule that keeps deleted EBS snapshots for 365 days, and restore any snapshot that someone deletes.

options.label: D
options.text: Lock each monthly snapshot in compliance mode for one year, without a cooling-off period, as soon as the company creates the snapshot.

items.stem: A company runs an application on one Amazon EC2 instance. The application keeps its data on an unencrypted Amazon EBS data volume. A new security policy requires the company to encrypt this data at rest. The company must also ensure that every new EBS volume that anyone creates in the Region from now on is encrypted. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on Amazon EBS encryption by default in the Region, and keep the AWS managed key as the default encryption key.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on Amazon EBS encryption by default in the Region, and wait for Amazon EBS to encrypt the existing volume in the background.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs every hour, finds new unencrypted volumes in the Region, and replaces each one with an encrypted copy.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Elastic Volumes to modify the existing volume in place, and turn on encryption while the volume stays attached to the running instance of the application.

options.label: E
options.text: Create a snapshot of the volume, copy the snapshot with encryption turned on, and replace the volume with a new volume from the copy.

items.stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in two AWS Regions, us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Teams in both Regions create new Amazon EBS volumes every day with their own scripts and templates. A new security policy requires that every new EBS volume in these two Regions is encrypted at rest. The company does not want to change the scripts and templates of the teams. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on Amazon EBS encryption by default in us-east-1 and in eu-west-1, and keep the AWS managed key of each Region as the default key.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a customer managed key in each Region, turn on Amazon EBS encryption by default in both Regions, and set each new key as the default key.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on Amazon EBS encryption by default in us-east-1 only, because the setting then applies to every Region of the account.

options.label: D
options.text: Run an AWS Lambda function every hour in each Region that finds unencrypted volumes and turns on encryption for each volume in place.

items.stem: A company must keep one Amazon EBS snapshot of a database volume for each month for seven years to meet a compliance rule. The snapshots are kept for long-term storage and are infrequently accessed. When an audit needs an old snapshot, a restore that takes up to three days is acceptable. The company currently keeps all of these monthly snapshots in the standard tier. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to keep these snapshots?

options.label: A
options.text: Delete every monthly snapshot except the most recent one, because the newest snapshot holds all of the data that the volume needs.

options.label: B
options.text: Copy the monthly snapshots into an Amazon S3 bucket through the Amazon S3 API, and store them in the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.

options.label: C
options.text: Move each monthly snapshot to the Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive tier after it is created, and restore it from there for an audit.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the monthly snapshots in the standard tier, and add a tag to each snapshot that marks it as part of the compliance record.

items.stem: A company runs a database on one Amazon EC2 instance that stores its data on one Amazon EBS volume. The company accepts the loss of up to one day of data and a recovery time of several hours. The company does not run any of its instances across multiple Availability Zones today. The company must be able to recover the database if the whole Region becomes unavailable. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the data on the current volume. After a failure, detach the volume and attach it to a new instance in another Availability Zone of the Region.

options.label: B
options.text: Take a daily snapshot of the volume. After a failure, create a volume from the latest snapshot in another Availability Zone of the same Region.

options.label: C
options.text: Take a daily snapshot and copy it to a second Region. Keep a standby instance running there, and restore each new copy to its volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Take a daily snapshot of the volume and copy it to a second Region. After a failure, create a volume from the copy there.
